clue.text: Harmful to be tired out in the mind

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of tired are rearranged

parts.note: something in the mind is mental, of the intellect

explanation.surface: A warning that getting exhausted in your head does you damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TIRED into DETRI; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detrimental causes damage or loss, so it is harmful.

clue.text: Expatriates run into warehouses

indicators.note: into says the run letter is placed inside the storage word

parts.note: depots are warehouses or storage buildings
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: People living abroad dash into storage buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expatriates' reads as a noun but is a verb: to expatriate someone is to banish them from their country.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatriate is to banish from one's homeland, the same as expelling a foreigner from a country.

clue.text: One eaves rest-room which is for hire

indicators.note: leaves says the one-letter piece departs from the lavatory word

parts.note: a rest-room is a toilet
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a public lavatory that can be rented.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as scanned reads 'eaves'; the wordplay needs 'leaves', I departing from TOILET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign reading this phrase advertises property available to rent, so it describes something for hire.

clue.text: Tipping in fashionable Reading, say?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a reading is one interpretation, a version of a text

explanation.surface: Tipping a stylish rendition, perhaps of a text in the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is capitalised to suggest the English town, but here it means an interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipping something over turns it upside down, which is an upending or overturning.

clue.text: It houses sewers in the Tuileries

indicators.note: in says the letters lie concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Drains run beneath the Tuileries gardens in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains but means people who sew; the needle case runs across 'thE TUIleries'.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and thread, so it holds the kit of those who stitch.

clue.text: Out clumsily in Test intensive coaching required

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: clumsily says the letters of out are put together awkwardly in a new order

explanation.surface: A batsman dismissed clumsily in a Test match needs serious batting lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' turns OUT into UTO, which goes inside TRIAL; 'required' is a link. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a session of close one-to-one teaching.

clue.text: For this tree, ring up about one

indicators.note: about says the turned word goes around the single letter
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Telephone round about this tree, one says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CALL into LLAC, which goes 'about' I. 'For this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a small tree or shrub with scented purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Must art suffer in bed?

indicators.note: suffer says the letters are put through a hard time and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether art has to be a torment even in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' sounds like somewhere to sleep, but it is a layer of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer of rock or soil, which geologists call a bed.

clue.text: Single girl in a leotard, for example

parts.note: single means one
piece is old slang for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: An unmarried young woman in a dancer's leotard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a garment made all in a single section, covering the body without separate top and bottom.

clue.text: European clear in this Olympic event

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
to vault is to leap clear of an obstacle

explanation.surface: A continental athlete clears the bar in this Olympic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pole-vaulting is a track and field event at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Craft put in the bin?

parts.note: a craft is a ship, here an ocean-going one, while the thing put in a bin is a plastic bag lining it

explanation.definitionFit: A liner is both a passenger ship and the bag fitted inside a rubbish bin.

clue.text: Sally's flask

definitions.meaning: a sally is a witty reply or quip
a laboratory vessel with a long downward-bent neck used for distilling

explanation.definitionFit: A retort is both a sharp rejoinder and a glass distilling vessel.

clue.text: Eccentric sort takes two drugs!

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An oddball takes a pair of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, a crank.

clue.text: Head keeps medal in everyday set of clothes

indicators.note: in says the medal letters go inside the clothes word

parts.note: a suit is a set of matching clothes for daily wear
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: The boss keeps a decoration on an ordinary outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is a link here; MM, the Military Medal, a British army award, sits inside SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the top or peak, so it is the head of a mountain.

clue.text: Part of Haydn's Clock Symphony?

parts.note: a symphony is divided into sections, and a clock has internal works that drive it; one word covers both

explanation.definitionFit: A symphony consists of several movements, and a clock's mechanism is also its movement.

clue.text: Light design of castle in Spain

parts.note: day is daylight
a dream is a plan or aspiration

explanation.surface: Light design for a castle in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. A castle in Spain is an idiom for an unrealistic fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle in Spain is a visionary scheme, a reverie that will never come true.

clue.text: River authority, a local target?

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, England
a board is a governing authority

explanation.surface: A river authority asks whether it is a target for local people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' means a pub, the British word for one's nearby bar, where darts are played.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the target thrown at in a game of darts, a pub game.

clue.text: More cuts ordered for shopper

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shopper asks for more pieces of meat to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests a butcher's order but rearranges MORE CUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is someone who buys from a shop.

clue.text: Vera on US trip is insatiable

indicators.note: trip says the letters stumble and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Vera's American holiday leaves her hungry for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ravenous is extremely hungry, impossible to satisfy.

clue.text: Turner which can be shown upside down without loss of effect

indicators.text: which can be shown upside down without loss of effect
indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means read from bottom to top, and the word stays the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A device that turns looks the same however you hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that revolves or makes things revolve.

clue.text: Keen to find some garden tools

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic gardener goes looking for gardening equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means eager or passionately enthusiastic.

clue.text: Mountaineer's first purchase?

parts.note: purchase means a grip or foothold, not shopping; a climber's first one is a small initial hold

explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a small foothold for climbing, and figuratively an initial advantage.

clue.text: Casual secretarial worker is tardy producing stencil

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
tardy means late

explanation.surface: An agency typist turns up late while making a stencil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'producing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern cut out as a guide, like a stencil.

clue.text: Classic place for a tailless insect

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter is removed

parts.note: a locust is a swarming grasshopper

explanation.surface: An ancient spot for a grasshopper missing its rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' means in the classical language Latin, where the word means a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is the Latin word for place, used in English for a site or position.

clue.text: Old boy, taking suet preparation, is slow-witted

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: preparation says the letters are worked into a new mix, as in cooking

explanation.surface: A former pupil making a suet pudding is rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparation' turns SUET into TUSE; 'taking' is a link. Suet is beef fat used in British puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means dull or slow to understand.

clue.text: Unfairly 'e hurt Arthur's Dad

indicators.note: unfairly says the letters are dealt with wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cockney complaint that he injured someone unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e is cockney for 'he'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon is the legendary father of King Arthur.

clue.text: Man, for example, lies about

indicators.note: about says the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who is a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island.

clue.text: Cordial note

definitions.meaning: a cordial is a restorative drink
the keynote, first degree of a musical scale

explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is both an invigorating drink and the keynote of a scale in music.

clue.text: Suit macho-style, this growth of hair?

indicators.note: style says the letters are styled, arranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: Would a macho look suit this growth on the upper lip?
explanation.definitionFit: A mustachio is a large elaborate moustache.

clue.text: County with tail-ender dismissed at wrong end-embarrassed-gave up!

indicators.note: the last letter is removed, as a last-order batsman is out

parts.note: Surrey is an English county

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of end are put in a disordered sequence

parts.note: red means flushed with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A county cricket side with its last batsman out at the wrong end, red-faced, concedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-ender dismissed' drops the Y of SURREY; 'wrong' makes NDE of END. A tail-ender is a weak batsman at the end of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or yield.
